  "reasoning": "All 16 final answers agree with the mathematics and their own captured worked solutions. Two worked solutions contain intermediate errors that do not change their final answers: q-118755 drops the factor 1/2 from the negative-endpoint logarithmic limit; q-51075 incorrectly labels its discussion of statement III as 'Statement II is true.' Mathematical verification: q-2389 substitutes u=x^3+7 and integrates u^(-1/2); q-72566 integrates the denominator's logarithmic derivative; q-4463 rationalizes to 1/(sqrt(x+4)+2), giving 1/4. q-7156 differentiates velocity to (5,4t). q-121920 gives acceleration (ln 2,-1/2) at t=1, whose norm is sqrt(4(ln 2)^2+1)/2. q-121917 gives acceleration (4,2) at pi/8, whose norm is 2sqrt(5). q-7165 and q-121926 differentiate position twice, giving (4t^3,6) and (2,4e^(2t+5)); q-121932 gives (-4,-18) at t=1. q-74403 reduces the integrand to 3cos(2x)+1. q-49605 substitutes u=ln x to obtain 8 times the integral of u from 2 to 4, which is 48. q-73659 substitutes u=log_7(4x), with dx/x=(ln 7)du. q-69893 has semiaxes 2 and 5, so its denominators are 4 and 25. q-118755 has divergent half-line integrals tending to -infinity and +infinity; its ordinary whole-line improper integral therefore diverges, despite a zero symmetric principal value. q-51075 has two half-line integrals diverging to +infinity. Thus both statement questions have only II and III true. q-118774 has antiderivative -e^(-x^2), with convergent half-line integrals -1 and 1, totaling 0. No earlier submission or grade is supplied; confirmation of MA's answers rests on the captured worked solutions.",
